desc.en: Red soil, yellow soil, sand, water pits — soil chemistry decides the colour of bronze patina.

title.en: Humid south vs. dry north

title.en: Quanzhou and Yuan blue-and-white

desc.zh: 色目商人、伊斯兰贸易、波斯钴料——泉州港是元青花诞生的地理支点。
desc.en: Semu merchants, Islamic trade, Persian cobalt — Quanzhou was the geographic pivot for Yuan blue-and-white.

desc.en: Yue, Longquan, Jingdezhen — why were China's most famous kilns all along the Yangtze?

title.en: How did the Grand Canal change porcelain distribution?

desc.zh: 一条人工河道，把南方的瓷器运到北方，也把北方的订单带回南方。
desc.en: A man-made waterway carried southern porcelain north — and northern orders back south.

title.zh: 铜矿与青铜时代
title.en: Copper mines and the Bronze Age

desc.zh: 长江中下游的铜矿带，决定了中国青铜文明的地理版图。
desc.en: The copper belt of the middle and lower Yangtze shaped the geographic map of Chinese bronze civilisation.

desc.en: From pre-war trade prosperity to post-war rebuilding, Singapore dealers witnessed a particular slice of the city's history.

desc.en: Nanyang migration, remittance letters, clan associations — these historical links brought Chinese antiques to Singapore.

title.zh: “珠山八友”是怎么回事？
title.en: Who were the Zhushan Eight Friends?

desc.en: A group of literati porcelain painters in Republican Jingdezhen who put Chinese painting onto porcelain plaques.

title.zh: 民国仿古为什么这么厉害？
title.en: Why was Republic-era antiquarianism so skilled?

desc.zh: 上海开埠、古董商网络、宫廷匠人流入民间——民国仿品至今仍能骗过很多人。
desc.en: Shanghai's opening, dealer networks, imperial craftsmen entering the private market — Republic fakes still fool many people today.

title.zh: 宣德炉为什么被仿了五百年？
title.en: Why has the Xuande censer been copied for 500 years?

desc.zh: 一批风磨铜、一份铸炉档案、一场大火——宣德炉的传说从诞生起就带着神秘。
desc.en: A batch of wind-milled copper, a casting record, a fire — the Xuande censer was mysterious from birth.

desc.en: Literati taste, imported hardwoods, and maritime prohibition — three seemingly unrelated factors shaped Ming furniture.

desc.en: Under the single-port policy, Guangzhou became the only exit for Chinese-Western porcelain trade.

desc.en: The Opium Wars, the Boxer indemnity, and foreign museum buying trips — three forces pushed Chinese antiques out into the world.

desc.en: Kashan, Isfahan, Hormuz — following the sea routes back to the source of that blue.

title.zh: 宋代五大名窑为什么都在河南河北？
title.en: Why were the Song's five great kilns all in the north?

desc.zh: 汝、官、哥、钧、定——五个名字背后，是北宋定都开封的地理密码。
desc.en: Ru, Guan, Ge, Jun, Ding — five names, and the geographic logic of the Northern Song capital at Kaifeng.

title.zh: 和田玉是怎么运到中原的？
title.en: How did Hetian jade reach the Central Plains?

desc.zh: 从于阗到长安，一条比丝绸之路更古老的玉石之路。
desc.en: From Khotan to Chang'an — a jade road older than the Silk Road itself.

title.zh: 唐代瓷器为什么突然变多？
title.en: Why did Tang ceramics suddenly multiply?

desc.zh: 安史之乱之后，中国的经济重心南移，瓷器第一次成为大众商品。
desc.en: After the An Lushan Rebellion, China's economic centre shifted south — and ceramics became mass-market for the first time.

title.en: Why did Jingdezhen become the porcelain capital?

desc.zh: 高岭土、昌江水运、松柴燃料——三样东西，缺一不可。
